item.title: Why the Gulf States Stay Loyal to the US
item.description: Washington does not seem to realize that it holds more leverage over the wealthy petro-monarchies of the Persian Gulf than vice versa. It should use it. The post Why the Gulf States Stay Loyal to the US appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Japan’s Fleet of F-35 Fighter Jets Is Growing. So Are Its Military Bases.
item.description: Japan now operates dozens of advanced F-35 stealth fighters—including the F-35B STOVL variant, based on its two quasi-aircraft carriers. The post Japan’s Fleet of F-35 Fighter Jets Is Growing. So Are Its Military Bases. appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Turkey Just Asked Putin to Take Back the S-400 Triumf Air Defense System
item.description: Turkey has kept the S-400 systems deactivated for nearly a decade as it has sought re-entry into the US-led F-35 program. The post Why Turkey Just Asked Putin to Take Back the S-400 Triumf Air Defense System appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Could Russia’s S-500 Air Defense System Be an “F-35 Killer”? Here’s What We Know
item.description: Russia has heaped praise on its new S-500 missile system, but it is still unclear if it can actually build the systems in meaningful numbers. The post Could Russia’s S-500 Air Defense System Be an “F-35 Killer”? Here’s What We Know appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: America Stole Iran’s Shahed Drone—and Is Now Copying It
item.description: The Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS) drone, now under development by the US Marine Corps, is a carbon copy of the Shahed drone. The post America Stole Iran’s Shahed Drone—and Is Now Copying It appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How Much Would a US Invasion of Venezuela Cost?
item.description: It is hard to calculate the cost of a US invasion of Venezuela—but if past wars are any guideline, a conservative estimate would be hundreds of billions of dollars. The post How Much Would a US Invasion of Venezuela Cost? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Britain Arms Ukraine Against Russia’s Drone Swarms
item.description: The UK has delivered more than 1,000 air defence missiles and over 250,000 rounds of air defence ammunition to Ukraine thus far in 2025. The post Britain Arms Ukraine Against Russia’s Drone Swarms appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Dark Eagle Hypersonic Missile Will Pierce China’s A2/AD Bubble
item.description: The Dark Eagle missile will allow the US Army to bypass current anti-access/area denial (A2/AD) umbrellas with ease. The post The Dark Eagle Hypersonic Missile Will Pierce China’s A2/AD Bubble appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Trump’s “Western Hemisphere Command” Is Just the Start of His New Plans
item.description: Trump’s national security strategy outlines a broad rethinking of American defense priorities—starting from the Western Hemisphere and branching outward. The post Trump’s “Western Hemisphere Command” Is Just the Start of His New Plans appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: On General Patton’s Death Anniversary, We Remember How He Inspires Even Today
item.description: Patton was not an ideal commander. But his fighting spirit was second to none—and continues to inspire military leaders in the United States today. The post On General Patton’s Death Anniversary, We Remember How He Inspires Even Today appeared first on The National Interest.
